title: Discovered consistently reproducible bug involving Windows shortcuts while using Keyboard Shortcut Mapping

status.label: Retest repeated Win+Home/End mappings on the current build
status.detail: The detailed v0.92.1 sequence reports repeated Win+Home/End mappings sometimes invoke native Win+Home behavior after focus changes, while Win+PgUp/PgDn mappings work.

judgment.rationale: The reporter provides exact Win+Home/End and Win+PgUp/PgDn mappings, focus change, and idle period across two laptops. Shortcut A fails after a mouse focus change and Windows native Win+Home behavior becomes visible. There is no current-build test or diagnostic archive; the detailed old sequence should be retested, not requested again.
evidence: PowerToys 0.92.1; Windows 11 build 26100 and Windows 10 XPS tested; elevated.
Shortcut A maps Win+Home/End to Ctrl+Win+Left/Right; Exact Match disabled and no chords.
Shortcut B maps Win+PgUp/PgDn to Ctrl+Win+Left; reporter says it works consistently.
After a mouse focus change Shortcut A may expose native Win+Home minimize/restore behavior; the report also describes an idle interval.
No comments or diagnostics are attached.
judgment.recommended_action: Repeat the documented sequence on v0.102.3001 and capture a fresh /bugreport immediately if Shortcut A still falls through after the focus change.

fix_assessment.rationale: If this still reproduces, Keyboard Manager may leave the OS-level Win chord active or lose remap state after the focus transition; the old report does not establish whether this remains in current code.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep repeated Win+Home/End remaps from falling through to Windows
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Repeated Win+Home/End may leave a modifier or remap state inconsistent after a mouse focus transition, allowing Windows native Win+Home behavior instead of the configured output.
plan: Run the documented Shortcut A sequence on v0.102.3001 with the mouse focus change.
Compare Shortcut B and the described idle interval to identify the failing state transition.
If current code reproduces, correct the remap or modifier cleanup path and add a focused regression test across focus changes.
verification: Repeated Shortcut A presses produce only Ctrl+Win+Left/Right and do not invoke native Win+Home.
Existing Shortcut B mappings remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The reproduction is detailed but from 0.92.1; native Windows behavior does not prove which Keyboard Manager transition causes it.

issue_context.summary: Repeated Win+Home/End remaps reportedly fall through to native Windows behavior after a mouse focus change.
known_information: The report documents exact mapping groups, focus change, idle wait, and two laptop keyboards.
The reporter distinguishes failing Win+Home/End from working Win+PgUp/PgDn.
inferences: A modifier/remap state issue across focus changes is possible but current behavior and mechanism are unconfirmed.
issue_context.analysis: The detailed sequence is sufficient for a maintainer to repeat. A current-build test is needed; request fresh diagnostics only if it still occurs.
initial_investigation: Read the full mapping and focus/idle reproduction.
Recorded that the reporter already compared two laptops and ruled out Fn-specific behavior.
Confirmed there is no current-build test or attached diagnostic.

comment.body:
Thanks for documenting the exact Shortcut A and Shortcut B mappings, the focus change, and the same result on two laptops. There is no need to restate those steps. The report is from v0.92.1, and the white outlines/native Win+Home behavior may be Windows receiving the original chord.

Could you please:
1. Repeat the documented sequence on v0.102.3001 without changing the mappings and report whether Shortcut A still fails after the mouse focus change while Shortcut B works.
2. If the current build still falls through to native Win+Home, comment /bugreport immediately after it happens, before restarting or changing the mapping.
This will determine whether current Keyboard Manager still loses the remap across the focus transition.
